summary: Intermittent 403 when submitting delegated access requests from Electron portal
description:
Issue summary: Several Support and Platform engineers intermittently receive 403 Forbidden when clicking 'Request Access' (delegated role request) from the Electron-based internal portal. The button appears to succeed for a moment (UI shows spinner) and then a toast "Request failed: 403" appears.

Impact: Affects internal tooling access flows for ~10% of requests during observed windows; prevents engineers from obtaining temporary delegated roles and blocks on-call runbook access. No reported customer-facing impact, but causes operational delays during incidents.

Observed characteristics: failures are intermittent (not tied to a single user), correlate with times of autoscaler events on the auth-proxy pool, and appear to surface only when users' requests route across upstream auth-proxy instances that have recently cycled. Requests routed to a warm auth-proxy instance succeed consistently.

Initial hypothesis: 403s caused by CSRF/session validation failure due to stale server-side session state / CSRF token cache being evicted or lost after memcached eviction or container restart; when load-balancer stickiness flips between backends the Electron portal submits a token that is no longer valid on the new backend.

Environment details: Electron v2.5.1 (internal); auth-proxy (k8s deployment auth-proxy-prod, HPA autoscaler triggers), session-store uses memcached-cluster-1 (managed), RBAC service v1.14.2. Okta SSO is the identity provider; session cookie is SameSite=None; auth-proxy sets an app-specific CSRF token in server-side cache keyed by session id.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Sign in to Electron portal (Okta SSO) and confirm role is unstaged for delegation.
2) Trigger a role delegation request via the portal UI (Request Access → choose role → submit).
3) Repeat submit while watching which auth-proxy pod handles requests (kubectl get pods -n auth | kubectl describe endpoints to correlate), or while an HPA-induced pod churn is happening.
4) Observe that some submissions return 403 and corresponding errors in auth-proxy logs; submissions routed to a different pod often succeed.
5) Reproduce window correlates with memcached evictions and k8s scaler events (scale up/down).
logs: auth-proxy[2026-03-12T15:14:21Z] WARN csrf: validation failed for session=abc123, expected token missing (cache-miss)
rbac-service[2026-03-12T15:14:21Z] INFO delegation-request denied user=leah.chen@redwood.com reason=csrf_validation_failed
ingress-lb[2026-03-12T15:14:22Z] INFO backend-change client_ip=10.32.5.18 from=auth-proxy-7ff4d -> auth-proxy-9d1c3
investigation_notes:
- Reproduced in staging by forcing auth-proxy pod recycle + memcached eviction; observed same 403 and csrf cache-miss entries.
- Correlation between HPA pod churn and higher 403 rate (spike from baseline 1% -> 12% during churn window).
- Session cookie binding is fine; issue is server-side CSRF cache keyed by session id and not replicated across instances.
- Auth-proxy currently uses local in-memory CSRF token cache fallback to memcached; memcached eviction/eviction race window leads to cache-miss and immediate 403.
- Electron client does not retry on 403; UX shows immediate failure.

Next steps: (1) Add request-level retry in Electron for transient 403s on delegation endpoints (short-term mitigation). (2) Update auth-proxy to persist CSRF tokens in a strongly-consistent store or implement double-submit cookie pattern to remove server-side dependency (design RFC). (3) Add metric + alert for csrf_cache_misses / delegation_403_rate. (4) Patch memcached eviction settings and review HPA cooldown to reduce chop frequency.
comments: Leah Chen (reporter) 2026-03-12: Noticed this during an on-call rotation when I couldn't request a delegated role after a pager. The portal showed the spinner and then 403 toast. I retried twice and then it worked once (after a minute).
Marco Ruiz (assignee) 2026-03-12: Confirmed similar traces in prod logs. Spun up a staging test to simulate HPA churn; can reproduce. Will prototype client-side retry while we design server fix.

SRE #internal-access 2026-03-12: Observed memcached slab rebalances during the same window; investigating eviction patterns. Suggest temporarily increasing memcached memory and adding eviction metrics.
Security 2026-03-13: CSRF change must preserve protection guarantees. Double-submit cookie approach acceptable but coordinate with security review.
